:JUDGMENT:
The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.7118/2019, MVC.7119/2019 and MVC.7120/2019 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ each for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Since all these Petitions arises out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 1911 2021 in MVC No.7118/2019, these three cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in all the Petitions are as under:
That on 09072019 at about 3.00 a.m. the Petitioners were shifting foundation stones from Kalikere village to Jangaalahalli in a tractor bearing No.KA07TA 0639, near Mudigere gate NH75 road, Mulbagal Taluk, Kola, a Oil Tanker bearing No.KA04AB5503 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the tractor in which petitioners were proceeding.
Due to the said impact, all the Petitioners sustained grievous injuries.
4. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7118/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
5. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7119/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
6. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7120/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

7. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioners were hale and healthy and they were working as agriculturist and daily wage labours and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
8.

The Petitioners of all the Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Oil Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA04AB5503 which is Manjunath.C vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72398784/
2 insured by the Respondent No.1 and owned with Respondent No.2.

9. In pursuance of service of notice, Respondent No.1 & 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and filed their respective Objection Statements.
10. In all the petitions, Respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further it has admitted that the Oil tanker bearing Reg. No.KA04AB5503 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending tanker.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in all the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
On these grounds, he has prayed to dismiss all the petitions.
11. In all the petitions, Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.

Further it is admitted that this respondent is the RC owner of the alleged offending Oil Tanker vehicle and it was insured with the first respondent vide policy No.0716033118P111152244 and the same was valid as on the date of accident and also the driver of the alleged offending tanker was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Further it contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor who was proceeding ahead of the Oil tanker in a zigzag manner and suddenly stopped his vehicle abruptly without giving any signals or indication to the vehicles coming to his behind and caused the accident.
Further it is contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary and proper parties as the owner and insurer of the tractor were not made as parties.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in all the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.

On these grounds,
it has prayed to dismiss all the petitions.
12. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES IN MVC No.7118/2019 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 09.07.2019 at about 3.00 a.m. Mudigere gate, NH75 road, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar,
in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Oil Tanker bearing No.KA--04 AB 5503?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?

On the other hand,
the Respondents have not adduced rebuttal evidence.

I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited, and materials available on record.

 REASONS  18. Issue No.1 in MVC.7118/2019, 7119/2019 &
7120/2019:
It is the case of the Petitioners that they sustained injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending Oil Tanker bearing No.KA04AB5503.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Oil Tanker.
19. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, Petitioners in all the cases have been examined as P.W.1 to PW.3 and they also examined two witnesses as P.W.4 & PW.5.
They got marked in total 29 documents.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 are the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch map, IMV report, MLC register and Charge Sheet.

20. I have carefully gone through the documents, it shows that on the complaint lodged by one Muniraju the case was registered against the driver of the offending Tanker bearing No.KA 04AB5503 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn the Spot Panchanama along with sketch map at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P3 is IMV Report wherein the Motor Vehicle Inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the Accident Register.

Ex.P5 is the True copy of Chargesheet shows that the driver of Oil Tanker bearing No.KA04AB5503 was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 of IPC r/w Section 177 of IMV Act.
21.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.3, the Learned Counsel for Respondents have cross examined the P.W.1 to PW.3 at length.
In the crossexamination, PW.1 to PW.3 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.
22. To rebut the evidence of PW.1 to PW.3, Respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.
Moreover, the Charge sheet is the material document which is filed against the driver of the offending tanker.
It is not in dispute that the charge sheet is not challenged by the driver of the offending tanker.

Such being the case when the documents speak for itself that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Oil tanker, any amount of oral evidence by way of suggestions during crossexamination of PW.1 to 3 denying the negligence of the driver of tanker cannot take away the case of the petitioners.
Hence, this tribunal is of the view the accident in question occurred as a result of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending oil tanker bearing Manjunath.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in all the cases in the "Affirmative".

23. Issue No. 2 in MVC.7118/2019 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending tanker by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
24. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 26 years.
He has produced her Aadhar card at Ex.P.6.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the Petitioner is 09031993.
The accident has taken place on 09072019.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 26 years, and the same is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
25. It is to be noted here that, according to the petitioner, he had sustained grievous injuries.

But,
the medical record produced by the Petitioner himself, i.e., Ex.P.13 Discharge summary shows that the Petitioner had sustained Multiple abrasion over face right leg and right hand which are simple in nature and also shows that Petitioner was admitted on 09072019 and got discharged on 1907 2019 and took conservative treatment.
26. In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.
But, the documents produced by the Petitioner shows that he had sustained simple injuries.
The evidence shows that the Petitioner had admitted in the hospital for 10 days and incurred expenditure of Rs.13,698/ for his treatment and other expenses.
27. It is not the case of the Petitioner that he has suffered from any permanent disability.
Admittedly, the Petitioner is aged about 26 years.

In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.
28. Issue No. 2 in MVC No.7119/2019 :
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending tanker by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
29. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 21 years.
He has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.8.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the Petitioner is 15011998.
The accident has taken place on 09072019.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 21 years, and the same is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
30. It is to be noted here that, according to the petitioner, he had sustained grievous injuries.

Petitioner has examined one Kishore M.R., Junior Executive, R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar as PW.4 who has produced case sheet and MLC register at Ex.P20 and Ex. P.23 which show that the Petitioner had sustained multiple abrasions over B/L hand and he was admitted on 09072019 and got discharged on 15072019.

In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.

33. Issue No. 2 in MVC No.7120/2019 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending oil tanker by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
34. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 18 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.10 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 10012001.
The accident took place on 09072019.
Hence, the age of the petitioner 18 years is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
35. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he is agriculturist and daily wage labour and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to substantiate the said fact.
No supportive documents are furnished to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/p.m.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
36. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
37.

The case sheet i.e., Ex.P21 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained right closed distal end radius fracture which is grievous in nature and he has also underwent surgery.
Further, P.W.5 has also reiterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.
38. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :

sentences.text: Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
40. The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 09072019 and discharged on 18072019 in R.L. Jalappa hospital.

41. Upon going through Ex.P15 i.e., the Discharge summaries shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient 09072019 and discharged on 18072019 in R.L. Jalappa hospital i.e.,
for 10 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 10 days.
42. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,000/ per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
43.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
44. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.20,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
He has produced 30 medical bills at Ex.P.16 amounting to Rs.27,210/.
I have gone through the medical bills.

Though suggestions are made to PW.1 during cross examination that the medical bills furnished are created for the purpose of this petition to claim higher compensation, the medical bills are not seriously disputed.
Upon consideration of the bills, they appears to be acceptable.
The acceptable medical bills totally amounting to Rs.27,210/.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.27,210/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

45. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not in a position to walk/stand/move without any help of others and he has to depend on others for his day to day work.
46. Further, the Petitioner got examined medical record officer as PW.4 and got marked Ex. P.21, 24 and 27 i.e., case sheet, MLC register and police intimation.

Further, he got marked Ex. P.28 and 29 i.e., clinical note and Xray.

He assessed disability of the right arm at 32%
and for whole body at 11%.
47.
PW.6 has reiterated the averments stated in the affidavit.
He has denied the suggestions put forth to him by the Learned Counsel for Petitioner.
In the crossexamination he admitted that he has not personally treated the Petitioner.
Further he admitted that fracture is united and implants are removed.
Further he has admitted that the petitioner can work with some difficulties and he denied that he has assessed disability at higher side.
48. Though the doctor who got examined as PW.5 assessed the whole body disability @ 11%.
It is to be noted that the injured/petitioner appeared before this court and got examined himself as PW.1 and deposed regarding the alleged incident.
He also subjected for cross examination and has given rational answers during his cross examination.
If this factor is taken into consideration, this Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed by PW.5 appears to be at the higher rate.

As such,
I am of the opinion that upon consideration of the injuries sustained by PW.3, if the disability is taken at the rate of 8% it would meet the ends of justice and equity.
49. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 13.

With multiplier of 13, income of Rs. 14,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,41,920 / (Rs. 14,000/ x 12 =
1,68,000/, Rs.1,68,000/x 18 x 8/100 = 2,41,920/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,41,920/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
50.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 27,210/
5. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 28,000/ up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,41,920/ Total Rs.3,92,130/ Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,92,130/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
51. Regarding Liability :

52. Issue No.3 in all the cases : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petitions filed by the Petitioners in MVC.7118/2019 MVC 7119/2019 and MVC and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act are hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7118/2019 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7119/2020 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7120/2020 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,92,130/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 in all the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in all the cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC.7120/2020, 80% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after proper identification and the remaining 20% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.

On deposit of the Award amount and  interest by the Respondent No.1 in  MVC.7118/2019 and MVC.7119/2019 since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioners by way of E Payment after their proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ respectively in all the cases.

The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.7118/2019, MVC.7119/2019 and MVC.7120/2019 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ each for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
4. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7118/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
5. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7119/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
6. Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.7120/2019 was shifted to R.L. Jalappa Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
7. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioners were hale and healthy and they were working as agriculturist and daily wage labours and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
8.
Further it contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor who was proceeding ahead of the Oil tanker in a zigzag manner and suddenly stopped his vehicle abruptly without giving any signals or indication to the vehicles coming to his behind and caused the accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
22. To rebut the evidence of PW.1 to PW.3, Respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.
Moreover, the Charge sheet is the material document which is filed against the driver of the offending tanker.
It is not in dispute that the charge sheet is not challenged by the driver of the offending tanker.
Such being the case when the documents speak for itself that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Oil tanker, any amount of oral evidence by way of suggestions during crossexamination of PW.1 to 3 denying the negligence of the driver of tanker cannot take away the case of the petitioners.
Hence, this tribunal is of the view the accident in question occurred as a result of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending oil tanker bearing Manjunath.

In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.
In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.
The accident took place on 09072019.
Hence, the age of the petitioner 18 years is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to substantiate the said fact.
No supportive documents are furnished to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/p.m.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
He also subjected for cross examination and has given rational answers during his cross examination.
If this factor is taken into consideration, this Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed by PW.5 appears to be at the higher rate.
As such,
I am of the opinion that upon consideration of the injuries sustained by PW.3, if the disability is taken at the rate of 8% it would meet the ends of justice and equity.

52. Issue No.3 in all the cases : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petitions filed by the Petitioners in MVC.7118/2019 MVC 7119/2019 and MVC and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7118/2019 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7119/2020 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.7120/2020 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,92,130/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 in all the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in all the cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC.7120/2020, 80% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after proper identification and the remaining 20% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.
On deposit of the Award amount and  interest by the Respondent No.1 in  MVC.7118/2019 and MVC.7119/2019 since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioners by way of E Payment after their proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ respectively in all the cases.
